Miracle Bleach for Autism?

By: Anna-Maria van Niekerk | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Miracle Mineral Solution, nothing more than household bleach, is touted as a cure for autism--a gut sanitiser that will cure from HIV to cancer now in SA from the US where it's discredited.

Summary:
Pioneered and discredited in America, MMS has now been brought to South Africa by prophets of the Founder Bishop Jim Humble form the Genesis Healing Church. Chlorine activated with citric acid to form a solution of chlorine dioxide is administered orally and also as regular enemas to children who have no say in the matter -- doctors studying the results of excreted bodily fluids report that what MMS disciples believe are dangerous parasites leaving the body, are in fact gut lining and worse.
We speak to adults with autism spectrum disorder and parents of children with autism who have been exposed to MMS.
Sold in workshops by the Genesis Church and aso online

Further information:
Miracle Mineral Supplement, often referred to as Miracle Mineral Solution, Master Mineral Solution, or MMS, is a toxic solution of 28% sodium chlorite in distilled water. The product contains essentially the same ingredient as industrial-strength bleach before "activation" with a food-grade acid.
The name was coined by Jim Humble in his 2006 self-published book, The Miracle Mineral Solution of the 21st Century.
MMS is falsely promoted as a cure for HIV, malaria, hepatitis viruses, the H1N1 flu virus, common colds, autism, acne, cancer, and much more. There have been no clinical trials to test these claims, which come only from anecdotal reports and Humble's book.
Autism is a neuro-developmental condition with no cure, whose cause is unknown. Autistic children struggle to communicate, and can be self-destructive.
US author Kerri Rivera has written a book promoting the substance as a gentle cure for autism.
Jenny Buckle or Reach Autism SA provides training about the product to other parents in sessions where attendees are carefully screened. Jenny says she has experienced the positive effects of MMS first hand -- she has triples with autism and she began dosing them with MMS after attending a course in the US in 2013.
Buckle said her children made miraculous improvements.
The science is clear – this treatment is dangerous say doctors like Louise Lindenberg who specialises in treatment for autism in Cape Town. Lindenberg has seen first hand how children have been harmed by MMS -- lab results prove it. One of the children she treated landed in hospital with diarrhoea, weight loss, dehydration and metabolic disturbances.
PRO-MMS AUTISM CASE STUDIES Parents who are in favour of the solution believe the liquid cleanses the body of pathogens or germs. A former assistant at a school for the autistic claims she was forced to administer the solution to two pupils. Parents who saw their children vomiting or in pain believed the treatment was "getting rid of the autism-inducing parasites".
The US Justice Department describes MMS, chlorine dioxide, as an "industrial chemical used as a pesticide; in fracking and waste-water treatment." A US court last year sentenced Louis Daniel Smith to 51 months in jail for selling the product as a medicine -- the first known jail sentence linked to MMS.
In Canada, the product was banned after someone nearly died after using it in 2008. The Guardian has described MMS as "extremely nasty stuff, and the medical advice given is that anyone who has this product should stop using it immediately and throw it away. In Canada it was banned after causing a life-threatening reaction."
In August 2009, a Mexican woman travelling with her American husband on their yacht in Vanuatu took MMS as a preventative for malaria. Within 15 minutes she was ill, and within twelve hours she was dead. The island nation's public prosecutor, Kayleen Tavoa, did not press any charges as there were no specific laws banning the importation of MMS, but advised, "While every case is assessed on its own merits, I advise that any person who misuses MMS in Vanuatu in the future would be likely to face prosecution for potentially serious criminal offences. No person should ever give MMS to another person to drink without advising them of what it is they are drinking and of the serious risks to health that may arise if they decide to drink the mixture
Complementary medicines activist and allergist Dr Harris Steinman, says selling an industrial solvent as a medicine is illegal. As defined in the Medicines Control Act, MMS is not a natural product or a registered medicine and it was therefore illegal to use it on children.

Press Release:


It’s little more than household bleach, but is touted as a cure for autism and a gut sanitiser that will cure almost anything from HIV to cancer. Pioneered but discredited in the US, the mineral solution has now been brought to South Africa where the mixture, containing chlorine dioxide, is being administered to children. But there have been no clinical trials to test this so-called 'miracle solution' and experts say it’s downright dangerous. Carte Blanche investigates these medical claims.

Script:


Autism rates have risen so much in the last few decades it’s been called an epidemic, known for baffling behaviour. Some experts blame vaccines and toxic environments for the brain development condition that hampers language and social engagement and causes hyper-sensitivity.

LOUISE LINDENBERG: The difficult thing with autism is that, if you’ve seen one person with autism, you’ve only seen one person with autism – you can’t blanket approach anything in autism.

While treating autism from an evidence-based, medical perspective, Cape Town-based Dr Louise Lindenberg also embraces alternative interventions, like diet or herbal remedies if they prove safe and effective for parents at their wits’ end. She says a child with autism is born every forty-five minutes in this country.

LOUISE LINDENBERG: From the medical perspective one would look at medications that could improve concentration, medications that can improve sleep… But then from a biomedical perspective and that’s more the field that I work in, we do tend to place a lot of emphasis on gastro intestinal health because we believe that that’s an underpinning for a lot of other things that can go wrong.

When patients brought her Miracle Mineral Solution, they said it expelled parasites that they believed caused their kids’ autism. It smelled like bleach and stripped the colour from fabric.

MMS is 22,4% sodium chlorite mixed in equal parts with a food acid to make chlorine dioxide, or CD.

LOUISE LINDENBERG: The treatment involves adding citric acid, which could be from lemons or lime, or hydrochloric acid to it to activate it as chlorine dioxide. Now chlorine dioxide is actually known to be an industrial bleach, or a water purification mechanism. And this is then administered to children with the diagnosis of autism.

The idea of administering CD in diluted drops by mouth, ear, nose and enema, was brought to Cape Town by Jenny Buckle, a mother of four boys, of whom three are twenty-year old triplets, all with autism.

When her triplets developed new difficult behavior three years ago, Jenny decided to seek help at the Autism One conference in Chicago.

She attended a lecture by Kerri Rivera, also a mother of an autistic boy, who claimed his ATEC score – or Autism Treatment Evaluation Checklist score was reversing thanks to CD/MMS.

JENNY BUCKLE: We were absolutely overwhelmed by the number of parents and their testimonies. Kerri Rivera – just launched her book; completely new novel information, meet her and literally come home with the book under your arm. And that’s how I was introduced to chlorine dioxide.

Jenny had founded an organization called REACH Autism, from where she counsels other parents. Back from Rivera’s presentation in 2013, Jenny introduced CD/MMS in her workshops, on her website and in their diet support group. She lined up four families from her circle to share their testimonies.

CHARA SWART: The difference with Christiaan on CD was from Day One.

CHRISTIAAN SWART: He used a new sentence and had a spontaneous, he had a pillow fight with his sister.

CHARA SWART: Stuff he’s never done.

CHRISTIAAN SWART: Day Three his sister told him bye and he said “bye sussie” – he never acknowledged anybody when they said hi or bye.

CHARA SWART: Christiaan was on the CD protocol for about a year and a half. And this year, which I never thought would happen, he’s back in school with a facilitator and for the first time in his young life he’s without any medication. A loving boy, and my whole heart.

SHENAAZ RAWOOT: We’ve been on CD from about December of 2013, he has improved a lot.

KHALIL RAWOOT: He never used to look at us directly and now he looks into your face, he hugs you.

SONIA WILKENS: Ek het ‘n kind wat gooi en breek en sulke goed…so drie ure…kon jy onmiddellik ‘n reaksie sien van ‘n kalmer kind.

HANLI LANGENHOVEN: He couldn’t speak at all which he can now do, he was socially, he didn’t have friends previously, now he is the most sociable person you can ever imagine. We were on CD for 2 years, we’re off it now…he’s lost his diagnosis, he’s not Autistic anymore, he’s in a normal school; attending a normal school, he’s joined the chess club…he’s got friends he’s just the most delightful boy you’ll ever meet.

Persuasive CD-water testimonies swept through the autism community. In Johannesburg, a teacher at a specialized autism school was told to give it to the principal’s child orally – he would get it by enema at home. She asked to stay anonymous.

TEACHER: The owner did some research and found out about Kerry Riviera, and then wanted to cure his son, because they believe that their autism is caused by bacteria or parasites in their bowels to bleach the autism away to get rid of the worms that cause it …the child would be getting about 540ml of this CD water within an hour and this could go on throughout the day. Which in the beginning came with a lot of restraint, holding him down and giving him this solution. All the diarrhea and vomiting – there were terrible side-effects, but this was seen as this is a good thing, because it shows that it’s working. I did some research…even if you just look on the first google page the entire thing is all about the wrongs of it and how it’s a hoax.

MMS is shrouded in controversy. It was coined in 1996 in America by former scientologist Jim Humble who claims he discovered it as a cure for malaria.

JIM HUMBLE, WEBSITE: When it turns yellow. Add water, mix it and drink it.

Bizarrely, to market his claims, Humble founded GENESIS TWO CHURCH OF HEALING – a non-religious organization that’s been described as a cult. Humble is self-appointed Archbishop and has devised a batch of MMS treatments he calls sacraments.

JIM HUMBLE, WEBSITE: Protocol 3000 is often used with protocol 2000. It is also used just as another way of getting MMS into your body.

Humble teaches CD/MMS cures from acne to ebola, because it oxidises pathogens, or bacteria.

His Bishop in Mexico, Kerri Rivera, developed the autism protocols, claiming on her website a total of 214 children have recovered. We asked Rivera for an interview on her claims. She dismissed it as yet another mainstream media effort intent on confusing people that CD is the same as household bleach.

Humble claims no deaths have been attributed to MMS and over 20-million people use it, but in 2010, an Australian woman was reported to have died after using it.

Soon after, the American Food and Drug Administration warned they’d received complaints of injury and CD/MMS was a “potent industrial bleach”, used for “stripping textiles” and “industrial water treatment”.

Last year, a US federal jury found Daniel Smith guilty for selling MMS as a cure for many diseases. He was convicted of conspiracy, smuggling, selling misbranded drugs and defrauding the country.

JIM HUMBLE, WEBSITE: This trial is also putting MMS on trial for the first time and we want to make it the last time.

Smith was sentenced to just over 4 years.

The Genesis church is growing in South Africa. We sent our undercover researcher Nomsa to the Hazyview branch on the pretext she was HIV positive and had just started ARVs.

Nomsa was charged R8500 for a three-day workshop where the Bishop Lesley Barbeau said she would learn how to mix CD/MMS for various treatments.

LESLEY BARBEAU: So it’s 20ml MMS per one litre, ok…they’re training here next door and we nearly gassed them out the last time.

Medical doctor and consumer activist Harris Steinman runs a website analyzing alternative medicines to help people discern false scientific claims.

HARRIS STEINMAN: All products that claim to have a physiological effect and are not food are regulated by the Medicines Control Council. Medicines Control Council produces the laws and also has to police and enforce those laws. At present in South Africa there’s very little policing and enforcing.

In the workshop, Nomsa was taught to mix MMS into softdrinks, smuggling it into hospitals to treat patients. She was told to drop her ARVS and start using CD/MMS.

NOMSA: She said I’m going to graduate to be a Bishop and I can have my own patients and my own lab, so I can start treating people. Also I can start doing my own seminars, and charge people.

HARRIS STEINMAN: They claim it targets bacteria, but your body is filled with beneficial bacteria. How do you know that it only targets the so-called bad bacteria? There has been no clinical research on the benefits of MMS on the body.

We asked Lesley Barbeau for an interview to clarify her promotion of an untested medicine.

JOHN WEBB: Lesley, it’s John Webb calling from Carte Blanche.

LESLEY BARBEAU: John, I’ve got nothing to say to Carte Blanche – that the reason I did not answer the email.

In Ireland, Fiona O’Leary, a woman with autism and two autistic children of her own, complained to the UK’s Medicines Regulatory Agency and the United Nations’ Committee on Rights of the Child.

JOHN WEBB: What raised the red flag for you?

FIONA O’LEARY, AUTISTIC RIGHTS TOGETHER: This product has been banned among some countries, Canada being one of those countries. There was warnings everywhere… that this was not to be ingested. As I delved further I discovered they were giving this orally on through to children, some babies actually as young as ten months old.

On Facebook groups parents would share and compare what they described as parasites or worms expelled from their kids’ bodies thanks to CD.

LOUISE LINDENBERG: I was fortunate to be able to have that investigated by the pathologists who reported that there were no parasites in their tests that they’d done and that it actually was the colon lining together with the probiotic flora and plant material and mucus that was coming off.

Cape Town Autism specialist James Laporta reported the matter to the Medicines Control Council when he saw the effects.

JAMES LAPORTA: From my experience seen a lot of patients been quite harmed by this. They either have diarrhea or dysentery which is blood in the stool…can cause liver damage. You can get kidney failure for diarrhea from enemas and CD MMS, but I think we need to keep a very balanced look at this. A lot of evidence is showing that it causes harm.

JOHN WEBB: Despite the dire diagnosis of MMS from our experts, our interviews have revealed parents who would do absolutely anything to help their kids.

We interviewed Reach Autism’s Jenny Buckle in February – she said her triplets seemed to do well on CD initially but one regressed a bit.

JENNY BUCKLE: Because there were Reach parents doing it, it appeared that I was doing the marketing – I never had any contact with people outside of Reach. I continued training; I’m not qualified as anything other than a mum, but my experience have worked with many, many families and so I believe that it is every family’s choice…I’m not someone who promotes it, because I don’t actually believe many families could manage it and I think like anything, if you get it wrong you could have potential side effects, absolutely.

After this interview a mother came forward to dispute Jenny’s version in her son’s case.

EX-CD MOM: He would scream and cry and cry and cry – he was miserable. I brought this to her attention – that he wasn’t doing well and she told me to up the CD dosage, so I upped the CD dosage and it didn’t work.

We asked to re-interview Jenny in April to clarify whether she promoted an untested medicine. Her husband James was present.

JENNY BUCKLE, I do not remember ever telling someone they should double dose, because I didn’t do it with my own kids, but again that was 3 years ago, so…I don’t know.

JOHN WEBB: How would you discuss MMS with people inside that group?

JENNY BUCKLE: No…

JAMES BUCKLE: How…that’s got nothing to do with anybody…it’s not promoting…

JOHN WEBB: Are you not prepared to delve more into that?

JAMES BUCKLE: Would we draw up somebody’s sheet and send it to them? Help them and advise them? Yes, absolutely. Did we promote it? No.

Conflict spiked when Fiona O’Leary visited South Africa last year to investigate CD/MMS in the autism community. Soon after, it was reported that South Africa’s Health Minister Dr Aaron Motsoaledi would have it investigated.

FIONA O’LEARY: It’s not just the bleach, it’s the invasion of these children’s privacy; the photographs that are taken of their children as they get off the toilet – the psychological damage. This is a long term damage for these children.

EX-CD MOM: I feel disgusting, I feel like a bad mother, I feel like I did a disservice to my child. I actually apologized to him.

As soon as she could, the Joburg teacher left the school that continues to use CD/MMS.

TEACHER: I’m very ashamed that I took part in this – I could have refused, or done other things…I didn’t though.

JOHN WEBB TO CAMERA: Even someone who was at the forefront of the MMS movement in this country, Jenny Buckle appears to have taken a step back – she readily admits that her belief in the substance isn’t as strong as it once was.

JOHN WEBB: Knowing what you know now, would you have administered it to your triplets?

JENNY BUCKLE: No, if I came face to face with the product now that I learned about it in the media, no I wouldn’t.

LOUISE LINDENBERG: If one looks at your Hippocratic oath as a doctor, one would not advocate that treatment because it’s harmful and it causes damage.

Pioneered but discredited in the US, the mineral solution has now been brought to South Africa where the mixture, containing chlorine dioxide, is being administered to children. But there have been no clinical trials to test this so-called 'miracle solution' and experts say it’s downright dangerous. Carte Blanche investigates these medical claims. Script: Autism rates have risen so much in the last few decades it’s been called an epidemic, known for baffling behaviour. Some experts blame vaccines and toxic environments for the brain development condition that hampers language and social engagement and causes hyper-sensitivity. LOUISE LINDENBERG: The difficult thing with autism is that, if you’ve seen one person with autism, you’ve only seen one person with autism – you can’t blanket approach anything in autism. While treating autism from an evidence-based, medical perspective, Cape Town-based Dr Louise Lindenberg also embraces alternative interventions, like diet or herbal remedies if they prove safe and effective for parents at their wits’ end. She says a child with autism is born every forty-five minutes in this country. LOUISE LINDENBERG: From the medical perspective one would look at medications that could improve concentration, medications that can improve sleep… But then from a biomedical perspective and that’s more the field that I work in, we do tend to place a lot of emphasis on gastro intestinal health because we believe that that’s an underpinning for a lot of other things that can go wrong. When patients brought her Miracle Mineral Solution, they said it expelled parasites that they believed caused their kids’ autism. It smelled like bleach and stripped the colour from fabric. MMS is 22,4% sodium chlorite mixed in equal parts with a food acid to make chlorine dioxide, or CD. LOUISE LINDENBERG: The treatment involves adding citric acid, which could be from lemons or lime, or hydrochloric acid to it to activate it as chlorine dioxide. Now chlorine dioxide is actually known to be an industrial bleach, or a water purification mechanism. And this is then administered to children with the diagnosis of autism. The idea of administering CD in diluted drops by mouth, ear, nose and enema, was brought to Cape Town by Jenny Buckle, a mother of four boys, of whom three are twenty-year old triplets, all with autism. When her triplets developed new difficult behavior three years ago, Jenny decided to seek help at the Autism One conference in Chicago. She attended a lecture by Kerri Rivera, also a mother of an autistic boy, who claimed his ATEC score – or Autism Treatment Evaluation Checklist score was reversing thanks to CD/MMS. JENNY BUCKLE: We were absolutely overwhelmed by the number of parents and their testimonies. Kerri Rivera – just launched her book; completely new novel information, meet her and literally come home with the book under your arm. And that’s how I was introduced to chlorine dioxide. Jenny had founded an organization called REACH Autism, from where she counsels other parents. Back from Rivera’s presentation in 2013, Jenny introduced CD/MMS in her workshops, on her website and in their diet support group. She lined up four families from her circle to share their testimonies. CHARA SWART: The difference with Christiaan on CD was from Day One. CHRISTIAAN SWART: He used a new sentence and had a spontaneous, he had a pillow fight with his sister. CHARA SWART: Stuff he’s never done. CHRISTIAAN SWART: Day Three his sister told him bye and he said “bye sussie” – he never acknowledged anybody when they said hi or bye. CHARA SWART: Christiaan was on the CD protocol for about a year and a half. And this year, which I never thought would happen, he’s back in school with a facilitator and for the first time in his young life he’s without any medication. A loving boy, and my whole heart. SHENAAZ RAWOOT: We’ve been on CD from about December of 2013, he has improved a lot. KHALIL RAWOOT: He never used to look at us directly and now he looks into your face, he hugs you. SONIA WILKENS: Ek het ‘n kind wat gooi en breek en sulke goed…so drie ure…kon jy onmiddellik ‘n reaksie sien van ‘n kalmer kind. HANLI LANGENHOVEN: He couldn’t speak at all which he can now do, he was socially, he didn’t have friends previously, now he is the most sociable person you can ever imagine. We were on CD for 2 years, we’re off it now…he’s lost his diagnosis, he’s not Autistic anymore, he’s in a normal school; attending a normal school, he’s joined the chess club…he’s got friends he’s just the most delightful boy you’ll ever meet. Persuasive CD-water testimonies swept through the autism community. In Johannesburg, a teacher at a specialized autism school was told to give it to the principal’s child orally – he would get it by enema at home. She asked to stay anonymous. TEACHER: The owner did some research and found out about Kerry Riviera, and then wanted to cure his son, because they believe that their autism is caused by bacteria or parasites in their bowels to bleach the autism away to get rid of the worms that cause it …the child would be getting about 540ml of this CD water within an hour and this could go on throughout the day. Which in the beginning came with a lot of restraint, holding him down and giving him this solution. All the diarrhea and vomiting – there were terrible side-effects, but this was seen as this is a good thing, because it shows that it’s working. I did some research…even if you just look on the first google page the entire thing is all about the wrongs of it and how it’s a hoax. MMS is shrouded in controversy. It was coined in 1996 in America by former scientologist Jim Humble who claims he discovered it as a cure for malaria. JIM HUMBLE, WEBSITE: When it turns yellow. Add water, mix it and drink it. Bizarrely, to market his claims, Humble founded GENESIS TWO CHURCH OF HEALING – a non-religious organization that’s been described as a cult. Humble is self-appointed Archbishop and has devised a batch of MMS treatments he calls sacraments. JIM HUMBLE, WEBSITE: Protocol 3000 is often used with protocol 2000. It is also used just as another way of getting MMS into your body. Humble teaches CD/MMS cures from acne to ebola, because it oxidises pathogens, or bacteria. His Bishop in Mexico, Kerri Rivera, developed the autism protocols, claiming on her website a total of 214 children have recovered. We asked Rivera for an interview on her claims. She dismissed it as yet another mainstream media effort intent on confusing people that CD is the same as household bleach. Humble claims no deaths have been attributed to MMS and over 20-million people use it, but in 2010, an Australian woman was reported to have died after using it. Soon after, the American Food and Drug Administration warned they’d received complaints of injury and CD/MMS was a “potent industrial bleach”, used for “stripping textiles” and “industrial water treatment”. Last year, a US federal jury found Daniel Smith guilty for selling MMS as a cure for many diseases. He was convicted of conspiracy, smuggling, selling misbranded drugs and defrauding the country. JIM HUMBLE, WEBSITE: This trial is also putting MMS on trial for the first time and we want to make it the last time. Smith was sentenced to just over 4 years. The Genesis church is growing in South Africa. We sent our undercover researcher Nomsa to the Hazyview branch on the pretext she was HIV positive and had just started ARVs. Nomsa was charged R8500 for a three-day workshop where the Bishop Lesley Barbeau said she would learn how to mix CD/MMS for various treatments. LESLEY BARBEAU: So it’s 20ml MMS per one litre, ok…they’re training here next door and we nearly gassed them out the last time. Medical doctor and consumer activist Harris Steinman runs a website analyzing alternative medicines to help people discern false scientific claims. HARRIS STEINMAN: All products that claim to have a physiological effect and are not food are regulated by the Medicines Control Council. Medicines Control Council produces the laws and also has to police and enforce those laws. At present in South Africa there’s very little policing and enforcing. In the workshop, Nomsa was taught to mix MMS into softdrinks, smuggling it into hospitals to treat patients. She was told to drop her ARVS and start using CD/MMS. NOMSA: She said I’m going to graduate to be a Bishop and I can have my own patients and my own lab, so I can start treating people. Also I can start doing my own seminars, and charge people. HARRIS STEINMAN: They claim it targets bacteria, but your body is filled with beneficial bacteria. How do you know that it only targets the so-called bad bacteria? There has been no clinical research on the benefits of MMS on the body. We asked Lesley Barbeau for an interview to clarify her promotion of an untested medicine. JOHN WEBB: Lesley, it’s John Webb calling from Carte Blanche. LESLEY BARBEAU: John, I’ve got nothing to say to Carte Blanche – that the reason I did not answer the email. In Ireland, Fiona O’Leary, a woman with autism and two autistic children of her own, complained to the UK’s Medicines Regulatory Agency and the United Nations’ Committee on Rights of the Child. JOHN WEBB: What raised the red flag for you? FIONA O’LEARY, AUTISTIC RIGHTS TOGETHER: This product has been banned among some countries, Canada being one of those countries. There was warnings everywhere… that this was not to be ingested. As I delved further I discovered they were giving this orally on through to children, some babies actually as young as ten months old. On Facebook groups parents would share and compare what they described as parasites or worms expelled from their kids’ bodies thanks to CD. LOUISE LINDENBERG: I was fortunate to be able to have that investigated by the pathologists who reported that there were no parasites in their tests that they’d done and that it actually was the colon lining together with the probiotic flora and plant material and mucus that was coming off. Cape Town Autism specialist James Laporta reported the matter to the Medicines Control Council when he saw the effects. JAMES LAPORTA: From my experience seen a lot of patients been quite harmed by this. They either have diarrhea or dysentery which is blood in the stool…can cause liver damage. You can get kidney failure for diarrhea from enemas and CD MMS, but I think we need to keep a very balanced look at this. A lot of evidence is showing that it causes harm. JOHN WEBB: Despite the dire diagnosis of MMS from our experts, our interviews have revealed parents who would do absolutely anything to help their kids. We interviewed Reach Autism’s Jenny Buckle in February – she said her triplets seemed to do well on CD initially but one regressed a bit. JENNY BUCKLE: Because there were Reach parents doing it, it appeared that I was doing the marketing – I never had any contact with people outside of Reach. I continued training; I’m not qualified as anything other than a mum, but my experience have worked with many, many families and so I believe that it is every family’s choice…I’m not someone who promotes it, because I don’t actually believe many families could manage it and I think like anything, if you get it wrong you could have potential side effects, absolutely. After this interview a mother came forward to dispute Jenny’s version in her son’s case. EX-CD MOM: He would scream and cry and cry and cry – he was miserable. I brought this to her attention – that he wasn’t doing well and she told me to up the CD dosage, so I upped the CD dosage and it didn’t work. We asked to re-interview Jenny in April to clarify whether she promoted an untested medicine. Her husband James was present. JENNY BUCKLE, I do not remember ever telling someone they should double dose, because I didn’t do it with my own kids, but again that was 3 years ago, so…I don’t know. JOHN WEBB: How would you discuss MMS with people inside that group? JENNY BUCKLE: No… JAMES BUCKLE: How…that’s got nothing to do with anybody…it’s not promoting… JOHN WEBB: Are you not prepared to delve more into that? JAMES BUCKLE: Would we draw up somebody’s sheet and send it to them? Help them and advise them? Yes, absolutely. Did we promote it? No. Conflict spiked when Fiona O’Leary visited South Africa last year to investigate CD/MMS in the autism community. Soon after, it was reported that South Africa’s Health Minister Dr Aaron Motsoaledi would have it investigated. FIONA O’LEARY: It’s not just the bleach, it’s the invasion of these children’s privacy; the photographs that are taken of their children as they get off the toilet – the psychological damage. This is a long term damage for these children. EX-CD MOM: I feel disgusting, I feel like a bad mother, I feel like I did a disservice to my child. I actually apologized to him. As soon as she could, the Joburg teacher left the school that continues to use CD/MMS. TEACHER: I’m very ashamed that I took part in this – I could have refused, or done other things…I didn’t though. JOHN WEBB TO CAMERA: Even someone who was at the forefront of the MMS movement in this country, Jenny Buckle appears to have taken a step back – she readily admits that her belief in the substance isn’t as strong as it once was. JOHN WEBB: Knowing what you know now, would you have administered it to your triplets? JENNY BUCKLE: No, if I came face to face with the product now that I learned about it in the media, no I wouldn’t. LOUISE LINDENBERG: If one looks at your Hippocratic oath as a doctor, one would not advocate that treatment because it’s harmful and it causes damage.

metadata.Summary: Pioneered and discredited in America, MMS has now been brought to South Africa by prophets of the Founder Bishop Jim Humble form the Genesis Healing Church. Chlorine activated with citric acid to form a solution of chlorine dioxide is administered orally and also as regular enemas to children who have no say in the matter -- doctors studying the results of excreted bodily fluids report that what MMS disciples believe are dangerous parasites leaving the body, are in fact gut lining and worse. We speak to adults with autism spectrum disorder and parents of children with autism who have been exposed to MMS. Sold in workshops by the Genesis Church and aso online
metadata.Further information: Miracle Mineral Supplement, often referred to as Miracle Mineral Solution, Master Mineral Solution, or MMS, is a toxic solution of 28% sodium chlorite in distilled water. The product contains essentially the same ingredient as industrial-strength bleach before "activation" with a food-grade acid. The name was coined by Jim Humble in his 2006 self-published book, The Miracle Mineral Solution of the 21st Century. MMS is falsely promoted as a cure for HIV, malaria, hepatitis viruses, the H1N1 flu virus, common colds, autism, acne, cancer, and much more. There have been no clinical trials to test these claims, which come only from anecdotal reports and Humble's book. Autism is a neuro-developmental condition with no cure, whose cause is unknown. Autistic children struggle to communicate, and can be self-destructive. US author Kerri Rivera has written a book promoting the substance as a gentle cure for autism. Jenny Buckle or Reach Autism SA provides training about the product to other parents in sessions where attendees are carefully screened. Jenny says she has experienced the positive effects of MMS first hand -- she has triples with autism and she began dosing them with MMS after attending a course in the US in 2013. Buckle said her children made miraculous improvements. The science is clear – this treatment is dangerous say doctors like Louise Lindenberg who specialises in treatment for autism in Cape Town. Lindenberg has seen first hand how children have been harmed by MMS -- lab results prove it. One of the children she treated landed in hospital with diarrhoea, weight loss, dehydration and metabolic disturbances. PRO-MMS AUTISM CASE STUDIES Parents who are in favour of the solution believe the liquid cleanses the body of pathogens or germs. A former assistant at a school for the autistic claims she was forced to administer the solution to two pupils. Parents who saw their children vomiting or in pain believed the treatment was "getting rid of the autism-inducing parasites". The US Justice Department describes MMS, chlorine dioxide, as an "industrial chemical used as a pesticide; in fracking and waste-water treatment." A US court last year sentenced Louis Daniel Smith to 51 months in jail for selling the product as a medicine -- the first known jail sentence linked to MMS. In Canada, the product was banned after someone nearly died after using it in 2008. The Guardian has described MMS as "extremely nasty stuff, and the medical advice given is that anyone who has this product should stop using it immediately and throw it away. In Canada it was banned after causing a life-threatening reaction." In August 2009, a Mexican woman travelling with her American husband on their yacht in Vanuatu took MMS as a preventative for malaria. Within 15 minutes she was ill, and within twelve hours she was dead. The island nation's public prosecutor, Kayleen Tavoa, did not press any charges as there were no specific laws banning the importation of MMS, but advised, "While every case is assessed on its own merits, I advise that any person who misuses MMS in Vanuatu in the future would be likely to face prosecution for potentially serious criminal offences. No person should ever give MMS to another person to drink without advising them of what it is they are drinking and of the serious risks to health that may arise if they decide to drink the mixture Complementary medicines activist and allergist Dr Harris Steinman, says selling an industrial solvent as a medicine is illegal. As defined in the Medicines Control Act, MMS is not a natural product or a registered medicine and it was therefore illegal to use it on children. - PRO-SOLUTION - PARENTS OF AFFECTED CHILDREN - DR.
